docs.title: Home
docs.text:
This is a project dedicated to a godot utility for mapmaking and tools.

The MapLoader is added to a project to allow the mapmaker to work for them.

FateMap is a standalone program for creating and editing these maps for a project.

docs.title: FMT Files
docs.text:
An FMT is a Fate MaTerial file. FateMap uses these files to store the info of any material a mesh can be given or loaded which the maploader and maker use to track and manage materials and texture options for a given map.

To add a new FMT to your project that the mapmaker can see, in your game project, add the .fmt file anywhere inside the FateMap/Imported/materials folder. The format is shown below.

name = NONE
material = Materials/Default/defaultMaterial.material
texture = Materials/Default/None.png
parameters = {}
tags = []

name is the name of the material as shown in the mapmaker

material can be a ShaderMaterial StandardMaterial or any other godot material.

texture is both the image shown in the mapmaker and the texture that is used as the albedo_texture of any materials.

parameters contains special info/additional parameters for the material (I.E. a step_sound = step_sound_file_path.wav)

tags are a tag used by the editor for setting if a material is skipped when compiling for rendering and/or collision.

all paths inside an FMT are read as relative to the Imported folder.

docs.title: Setting up for usage
docs.text:
An FMT file works in the mapmaker(NOT THE MAPLOADER) regardless of if the Hashmap file is updated or not. to update the hashmap under Project>Tools you'll see update FMT hashmap. It will get all fmt files and map their hash to their locations.

This step is necessary anytime you add a new FMT file to allow the maploader to access them.

docs.title: MapLoader
docs.text:
The maploader for FateMaps is a set of resources you drag and drop into your project to allow the mapmaker to create maps for it.

MapLoader Repository

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Once you install and add them to your project they should appear as follows.

Any 3d models you intend to place on a map using the map maker are placed into the Models folder. Any textures/materials you intend to apply to the map in the mapmaker should be placed into Materials folder. You must create a .FMT file for the mapmaker to use them. FMT

Once added, go into the FateMap/decompilers/compiled folder. depending on versions, you may have more loaders. different version loaders are not guaranteed to work on different versions of maps. Add a node3D to your scene in Godot and give it the loader's script. it should have a parameter whe you select it for a target file. If you already have a compiled .fatemap file you can set it to the file path for it. A version mismatch can cause it to fail to load if you try. Otherwise, loading a map in the editor or game will recreate the map with all the compile settings used.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
MapMaker Repository

After installing and launching, you'll see a top bar. Select the folder of another Godot project with the maploader added to it. If it has any maps in FateMap/maps/Editing they will show up. If not you will only see New Map. Make sure your target project has been set up as well. setting up a project

docs.title: Map files
docs.text: The mapmaker is meant as a frontend to creating/modifying maps .FMPE files. A compiled map becomes a .fatemap and is a different format. .FMPE files keep the full data and are a larger file size than .fatemap files. .fatemap files remove unneeded data that is only required during editing to reduce load time and file size.
